name: Motor unit and skeletal muscle
summary: A motor unit is one anterior horn cell, its axon and all the muscle fibers it innervates, from a few fibers in the extraocular muscles to over a thousand in gastrocnemius. Force is graded by recruiting units in order of size and by increasing their firing rate. This is the framework of electromyography: neurogenic disease loses units and enlarges the survivors by collateral reinnervation (large, long, polyphasic potentials with reduced recruitment), while myopathic disease loses fibers within units (small, short, polyphasic potentials with early recruitment). Clinically, the motor unit is the lower motor neuron, and its failure produces weakness with wasting, fasciculations, hypotonia and lost reflexes.

anatomy.location: Anterior horn cell in the spinal gray matter or brainstem motor nucleus, axon in the ventral root and peripheral nerve, terminal branches at the end plates of muscle fibers scattered through the muscle.

subdivisions.name: Type I (slow, oxidative) units
subdivisions.note: small, fatigue-resistant, recruited first; postural muscles

subdivisions.name: Type II (fast) units
subdivisions.note: large, glycolytic, recruited later for power

subdivisions.name: Muscle spindle and Golgi tendon organ
subdivisions.note: sensory feedback that sets tone and the stretch reflex; gamma motor neurons adjust spindle sensitivity

function: Generation of muscle force under voluntary and reflex control; the size principle of recruitment; maintenance of tone through the stretch reflex loop.

bestView.label: cervical cord: anterior horn cells are the motor unit's origin

imaging.normalAppearance: Muscle MRI (T1 for fatty replacement, STIR for edema) shows the pattern of involvement: selective muscles in dystrophies and myopathies, diffuse edema in myositis, denervation edema in the territory of a nerve or root; muscle ultrasound shows increased echogenicity.

pathology.finding: Symmetric STIR-bright edema of proximal muscles, later fatty atrophy; guides biopsy site.
Selective fatty replacement of specific muscles (e.g. adductors and hamstrings) on T1 with characteriztic patterns per gene.
STIR edema of muscles sharing a nerve or root, then atrophy.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Muscle MRI; EMG; creatine kinase; biopsy

lesionEffects.deficit: Weakness with wasting, fasciculations, hypotonia and reduced reflexes
Proximal weakness with preserved reflexes and no fasciculations

lesionEffects.mechanism: Irritable motor units in neurogenic disease

examination: Distribution: proximal (myopathy) versus distal (neuropathy) versus mixed asymmetric (motor neuron disease)
Look for fasciculations at rest in several muscles
Gower sign and neck flexion power
pearls: Proximal symmetric weakness with normal sensation and preserved reflexes is muscle; distal weakness with sensory loss is nerve; asymmetric weakness with fasciculations and brisk reflexes is motor neuron disease
EMG asks one question: are the units big and few (nerve) or small and many (muscle)?
